text:
Sam K: Quick sync — proposing we converge the runtime-delta surface that sits between Hosted/Dedicated/Private. current adapter complexity is killing followups. thoughts?
Anya L: yup, we should. can you sketch the minimal surface you want?
Sam K: thinking of a tiny "delta manifest": a JSON blob that lists only differences from the canonical hosted behavior (features, req/resp hooks, auth expectations). example: 
```json
{
  "capabilities": ["kv-cache", "kv-ttl"],
  "auth": { "type": "kms", "expectation": "signed-token" },
  "max_sequence": 8192
}
```
Mike R: that helps. two quick tradeoffs: discovery vs explicit manifest. discovery is flexible but adds runtime probing. explicit manifests reduce runtime negotiation but require strict publishing/versioning.
Elaine Z: ops concerns: manifests must be signed/versioned and easy to fetch in air-gapped Private. also smaller manifest = easier to audit.
Anya L: agree on signing. also we need a compatibility fallback policy: if runtime asks for a capability that's missing, how do we degrade? auto-fallback to hosted variant? limited quota? circuit-break?
Sam K: proposal: fallback policy is part of manifest metadata. default = "graceful-degrade" which maps to defined fallbacks in control-plane. explicit flag can set "reject" for hard failures.
devex-bot: note: will update SDK docs if manifest shape is accepted.
Mike R: implementation note: adapters should implement a two-step handshake: fetch manifest (or use cached), validate signature, then do capability negotation. handshake must be idempotent and cheap.
Elaine Z: telemetry: emit a metric 'adapter.manifest.version' + gauge for capabilities present. also expose a probe for mis-negotiation frequency.
Sam K: another tradeoff: how big should the manifest be? small = easier but might force more roundtrips for optional features. maybe allow optional extension blobs stored by reference (s3/url) so manifest stays small.
Anya L: +1 on reference blobs. but Private deployments won't allow external fetches; so allow inline or sealed artifact. add `artifact_refs` with {type: "inline" | "url" | "bundle"}.
Mike R: testing: we need a harness that can simulate Hosted behavior, Dedicated limited-capabilities, and Private with explicit KMS differences. can we reuse existing runtime-infra tests?
Sam K: yes, add a 'delta-matrix' test generator that produces permutations of capabilities to run quick end-to-end checks. keep it cheap (unit+smoke).
Elaine Z: rollout: manifest v1 behind feature-flag. start with non-breaking capabilities (telemetry flavors, kv-ttl, batch sizes). avoid putting auth or billing semantics in v1.
Mike R: versioning scheme: semantic-ish, "v1.0", but include commit sha for audit. manifest must include `min_controlplane_version` to avoid subtle protocol mismatches.
Anya L: can we fold this into the existing adapter registry? I'd rather not double-maintain. registry entry -> manifest pointer.
Sam K: yes, registry should reference manifest pointer (and store signed copy). control-plane keeps authoritative copies for Hosted and Dedicated; Private can upload their sealed manifest during onboarding.
devex-bot: checklist generated: [update SDK handshake, add manifest schema, add signing CLI, update registry model, add matrix tests, docs].
Sam K: open question: do we allow adapters to dynamically advertise emergent capabilities (eg runtime-compiled kernels) after handshake? could break determinism.
Mike R: prefer static within session. dynamic capabilities ok between sessions but must bump manifest version and re-roll handshake for long-lived connections.
Anya L: ops: add a periodic revalidate job for long-running nodes to re-fetch manifest every N hours or on event. avoid spamming in Private (configurable).
Elaine Z: security: manifest signing keys lifecycle must be in KMS with rotation support. include fingerprint in registry so we can detect rogue manifests.
Sam K: action items: I'll draft manifest schema + fallback policy RFC. Mike will prototype handshake flow in runtime-adapter repo. Anya to adjust registry model. Elaine to outline signing/ops process.
ops-bot: Created ticket ARCH-1289: "delta-manifest: schema + handshake prototype" and assigned to Sam, Mike, Anya, Elaine. ETA end-of-next-week. :white_check_mark:
Sam K: thanks — will post RFC link once draft is up. low-priority nit: avoid the word "adapter" in docs when possible, use "runtime bridge" — helps non-arch folks.
Anya L: noted.
Mike R: small snippet for handshake (pseudo):
```
client -> GET /manifest  (validate signature)
client -> POST /negotiate {capabilities: [..]}
server -> 200 {accepted: [..], fallback: {...}}
```
Sam K: perfect. last thing: keep manifest readable and stable; this will be our single source for diffing envs in incident debug.
Elaine Z: agreed. I'll add logpoint guidelines in the ops runbook.
Sam K: closing for now — will @channel in a follow-up when RFC lands.
